_comment: Scenario-staged rout-then-ANNIHILATION demo: a lone low-morale (1) player infantry block of 12 is charged head-on by two 12-horse cavalry troops and BREAKS -- it enters routing (drawn faded) and flees. The squadrons are shallow and spawn close so their facing-front is in spatha reach at regiment contact. Routing units are still valid combat targets, and the cavalry (8.5 m/s sprint) are faster than the fleeing infantry (4.0 m/s sprint, 1.3 x that in flight), so pursuit is relentless: each routed man runs on his own from the riders he sees toward his own back edge (SoldierFlightStep), the runners scatter, and each rider rides at the runner nearest him and cuts him down on the move (SoldierPursuitStep; at Cannae the Numidian horse pursued the fleeing Roman cavalry and cut most of them down, Polybius 3.116). The casualties keep its morale from recovering, so it never rallies and is ANNIHILATED (soldiers reach zero) rather than escaping or rallying. The scene runs on a custom tall map (field 1600x2400, flat) with every actor staged in the deep south, so the flight has room; a second, safe player unit (140 Spearmen) stays in the fight so the battle doesn't declare defeat the instant the infantry routs. Measured with dense 2-tick FULL dumps on seeds 0 to 4, 2026-11-13 on #1949's branch: it routs by tick 100 and is still routing at tick 250 (pinned) with 3 to 10 of its 12 men left; the lead squadron (uid 3) is after it (target_enemy_uid 0) inside ticks 200 to 300 on every seed (pinned); and the last runner falls at tick 492 on the clip's own seed (seed 0), 446 on seed 1, 276 on seed 2, 590 on seed 3 and 640 on seed 4 (absent inside ticks 250 to 1200, pinned). On main c36560fa it was caught at tick 420, fought on the move to tick 542 and cut down between ticks 648 and 650. The pins were: ROUTING at tick 540, uid 3 targeting it and engaged in melee inside ticks 480 to 600, and gone inside ticks 610 to 700. The bottom-up flight and the riders' own pursuit (#1949) run it down earlier on four seeds and about as late on one, so the windows move to cover every seed, and the engaged pin is retired: riders who cut runners down on the move are not a block engaged in melee. Camera frames the clash and then pans with the chase (website/tools/demo-catalog.sh records 360 frames at 30 fps, to tick 720, which shows the kill on every seed). No player input needed. (A unit that truly breaks free instead recovers cleanly -- see test/unit/test_morale_recovery_demo_scenario.gd for that case in isolation.)

follow_error.reason: This is a regression from main, accepted on #1949's branch. follow_error reads the two cavalry troops, sustained, late in their long march on the Spearmen (target uid 1), long after their chase ended, on seed 3: uid2 71.92 and uid3 153.73 against 30. On seeds 0, 1, 2 and 4 uid2 reads at most 29.3, 29.2, 10.0 and 29.4 and uid3 at most 61.8, 29.4, 11.4 and 29.5 without failing (dense 2-tick FULL dumps, measured 2026-11-14). Why it regresses: the riders chase the runners down man by man, so when the chase ends they stand scattered over up to 450 wu, and the troop forms up where they stand with its grid at their centroid and marches on at once. A rider who ends up ahead of the block or beside it is sent round by the formed arrival's flank-and-rear corridor (SoldierBodies._corridor_to_slot), whose waypoint moves with the marching block, so he rides alongside it and does not close: at tick 902 on seed 3 one rider still stood 240 wu off his place. On main the troop pursued as a block and was never scattered. Accepted for now because the scatter is the bottom-up pursuit #1949 asks for; the riders rallying on the standard before the troop marches on is the follow-up. The tick cut-offs below were measured 2026-11-13. Analysing seed 3's dump cut off at successive ticks, uid2 passes through tick 900 and fails by 1000, and uid3 passes through 900 and fails by 910. uid3 ended its chase and re-formed where its riders stood at tick 375, its men up to 450 wu apart; it marched on the Spearmen at 34 wu/s from then on, and at 902 a rider still stood 240 wu off his place. The failing samples are the first judged ones after the re-form's transit window closes. The branch's previous head 433ac98a reads the same way, uid3 failing at 105.16 by tick 900. Main c36560fa drifts on the same march: with this clip's state ticks run on main, uid2 reads 59.3, 59.3 and 58.3 on seeds 0, 1 and 2, and uid3 about 32 on seed 3: a long march drifts on main too (#1983), but far less than this branch's scattered re-form.
